May 14th 2027

The Dutch team flew out to Port Louis today. I met them at the airport around lunchtime. They were easy to spot, a large group of tired and confused looking Europeans. When they were finally able to find me, I gave them a wave to come over. When they came over, they seemed to be led by Anna. When she reached me she ignored my outstretched hand went in for a hug. Certainly unexpected, but I wouldn't say it was unpleasant! She looked a little sheepish as she pulled out of the embrace. She then introduced herself more formally. It turns out that the leader of the Dutch team, Dr Pieters, had pulled out due to family reasons. Anna had been appointed the head of the team in his absence.

After pleasantries were exchanged, I led them to the minibus. I then took them to a fish restraunt on the harbour for some lunch. After we had something to eat, I took them back to the hotel to recover from the 12 hour flight. We met up a few hours later in the hotel bar, along with some of the Hong Kong team. I spent a lot of the night introducing myself and the rest of the researchers to the new arrivals. Although towards the end of the night I spent quite a bit of time with Anna, exchanging memories of our time at university in the Netherlands. It's good to see her again.

May 27th 2027

Both the German and Congolese teams arrived yesterday. I had gotten stuck in traffic while going to pick them up. It turns out that the two teams had met eachother while waiting for me and they had already acquainted themselves with eachother. When I couldn't find them at the gate, I went looking for them and eventually found them in the airport bar. Looking forward to looking forward to working with both teams.

June 7th 2027

The research outpost has been fully built. However, a major wiring fault means it won't be operational for a while. God dammit Pierre! On the bright side, the lab equipment for HQ has been delivered and installed as planned. Not long now before we set off, so excited!

June 27th 2027

It turns out it wasn't just the electrics they messed up, it was the water as well. So it took much longer than expected. But it's all done now. I've just finished the first formal brief to the team. I outlined any dangers and precautions to take such as dehydration and insect bites. I also told everyone of the plans for the first few weeks while we are there. We'll take the first week to settle in. The following weeks will involve exploring each of the islands before going into more advanced research. This is it, it's actually happening. We're leaving on the 5th July.
